items.text: Its futuristic Thailand is portrayed as a simulation city, a concept from within the musician that Thailand inspired.
items.why: Overview: 'a futuristic Thailand is portrayed as a simulation city ... it is a concept from within him that was inspired there'. Reuses the eight-word run 'futuristic Thailand is portrayed as a simulation city'.

items.text: August 2, 1995
items.why: Infobox: 'Released: August 2, 1995'.

items.text: August 1994 to March 1995, in Yokohama, Karuizawa, Bangkok and Tokyo
items.why: Infobox: 'Recorded: August 1994 – March 1995'; studios in Yokohama, Karuizawa, Bangkok and Tokyo.

items.text: Susumu Hirasawa, Yūichi Kenjo
items.why: Infobox: 'Producer: Susumu Hirasawa Yūichi Kenjo ( co. )' (Kenjo is co-producer).

items.text: Polydor K.K.
items.why: Infobox: 'Label: Polydor K.K.'.

items.text: In 1994 his neighbour, Doll Magazine editor-in-chief Mikio Moriwaki, suggested he try a Pink Floyd-style sound for his next record.
items.why: Overview: 'In 1994, Susumu Hirasawa got the suggestion to try a Pink Floyd -like sound for his next solo album from his neighbor, Doll Magazine editor-in-chief Mikio Moriwaki'.

items.text: The first plan was a '90s take on The Dark Side of the Moon, covering much the same ground as Virtual Rabbit.
items.why: Overview: 'His original plan was to make a '90s version of The Dark Side of the Moon, which would cover similar ground to Virtual Rabbit'.

items.text: Later, he came up with the World Inspection Tour, a role-playing game held overseas for members of his fan club, Hirasawa Bypass.
items.why: Overview: 'the World Inspection Tour ..., a role-playing game held in an overseas country for members of his official fan club Hirasawa Bypass'.

items.text: The tour was set for Phuket in Thailand, since the flight was short and the place had little Japanese tourism.
items.why: Overview: 'decided that it would happen in the Thai city of Phuket, since the airplane trip would be short and it didn't have a lot of Japanese tourism'.

items.text: On that trial visit he had no clear idea, only a rough picture of the Vietnam War.
items.why: Overview: 'Hirasawa took a trial visit ... He had no idea what to expect and had something like the Vietnam War in mind'.

items.text: One night at the Simon Cabaret, where every performer was kathoey, shaped how he saw Thai culture.
items.why: Overview: 'a show at the Simon Cabaret, performed by a cast consisting entirely of the country's Kathoey people, and that was formative on his impression of Thai culture'.

items.text: Hirasawa did not trust the Thai studio with his gear, so he brought only instrumental 24-track recordings on analog reels to Thailand.
items.why: Overview: 'Hirasawa's lack of trust of their dealing with his gear, he only brought 24-track instrumental recordings on reels of analog tape'.

items.text: There he recorded only vocals over four days, his own and those of Thai performers.
items.why: Overview: 'the only material recorded there were vocals both his and from Thai performers over a 4-day span'.

items.text: Although he was not fluent in Thai, he wrote some lyrics by cross-referencing four language guidebooks.
items.why: Overview: 'Although Hirasawa is not proficient in Thai, he wrote some of the lyrics in it by cross-referencing four language guidebooks'.

items.text: What he first wrote meant something other than he intended, so he rewrote lyrics and melodies on the spot.
items.why: Overview: 'the meaning ... was completely different from what he wanted to convey, which led to on-the-fly rewriting of both lyrics and melodies'.

items.text: Masanori Chinzei handled recording and mixing, and Keiko Ueda mastered it.
items.why: Personnel: 'Masanori Chinzei - recording, mixing'; 'Keiko Ueda - mastering'.

items.text: The booklet was shot in Thailand, and it is the only one of his solo albums where he is not the only person pictured.
items.why: Overview: 'The photoshoot for the album's booklet took place in Thailand and is the only one made for a Hirasawa solo album where he isn't the only person in the photos'.

items.text: It was his fifth studio album and his last record with Polydor.
items.why: Lead: 'the fifth studio album ... This is his last record with Polydor'.

items.text: He later switched labels to Nippon Columbia.
items.why: Lead: 'he would later switch record labels to Nippon Columbia'.

items.text: Miss N. of the Phuket Simon Cabaret narrates it, and its lyrics are by her and Hirasawa.
items.why: Personnel: 'Miss N. (Phuket Simon Cabaret) - narration on "Recall"'; Track listing: 'except "Recall", "Sim City" and "Prologue", with lyrics by Hirasawa and Miss N.'. Title matches.

items.text: Wisakha Fraytes sings on it, and Miss N. narrates it without a credit.
items.why: Personnel: 'Wisakha Fraytes - vocals on "Sim City"'; Miss N. narration on '"Sim City" (uncredited)'. Title matches.

items.text: Miss N. narrates this track as well.
items.why: Personnel: Miss N. narration on '"Prologue"'. Title matches.

missed: That 'Sim City' plays on 'Siam City' and that Hirasawa calls the result 'fake' world music simulating no particular place; and the cover image of Miss N. wearing a veil made of MIDI cables.
